generator.command: uv run --no-project --with xraylib --with spekpy --with numpy python scripts/make_tables.py

libraries.spekpy_dependency_note: spekpy requires scipy and matplotlib; resolved by uv (versions not pinned by this script)

installed_package_statement: xraylib: a library for X-ray--matter interactions
xraylib.data_lineage: UNVERIFIED: the installed package does not state which tabulation underlies CS_Total/CS_Total_CP; its documentation is an external wiki that was not read offline.

spekpy.installed_metadata_summary: A Python software toolkit for modelling the x-ray spectra from x-ray tubes
mu_data_source_doc: :param string: mu_data_source (default: depends on physics model)
spekpy.chosen: physics='casim' (SpekPy v2 casim model), mu_data_source='pene' (SpekPy default for casim)
spekpy.data_lineage: UNVERIFIED: the bundled files are named pene_mu.dat and nist_mu.dat; their original source was not stated in the installed docs.
spekpy.validation_reference: Bujila R, Omar A, Poludniowski G. Phys Med 2020;75:44-54 (cited in the installed METADATA; not re-read)

spectra.model: SpekPy tungsten reflection target, 12 deg anode angle, kVp 80 and 120, mas=1, focus-to-detector 100 cm, native SpekPy defaults otherwise
spectra.filtration: 2.5 mm Al total (SpekPy filter thickness unit is mm; checked against xraylib Al mu/rho at 30 keV)
spectra.inherent_filtration: none added (SpekPy default filtration list is empty); real tube window/oil not modelled
spectra.rebinning: native 0.5 keV bins are summed into 1 keV bins; bin n covers [n-0.5, n+0.5) and holds native bins with centre in that range; values are photons per 1 keV bin
spectra.normalisation: SpekPy native, as returned by get_spectrum(edges=False, flu=True, diff=True) times 0.5 keV. Absolute normalisation vs a physical air kerma or fluence: UNVERIFIED. Consumers must rescale to a target count.

attenuation.quantity: total mass attenuation coefficient incl. coherent scattering, cm^2/g, at grid points
attenuation.water: xraylib CS_Total_CP('H2O', E): compound composition H2O, density 1.0 g/cm^3 reference
attenuation.iodine: xraylib CS_Total(53, E); ref density 4.93 g/cm^3 (solid I2, elemental)
attenuation.calcium: xraylib CS_Total(20, E); ref density 1.55 g/cm^3 (Ca metal, elemental)

nist_spot_checks.reason_for_rtol: NIST and xraylib tabulations differ in data lineage; 2% is a loose consistency bound, not a precision claim

known_limitations: The 1 keV grid under-resolves the iodine K-edge at 33.17 keV. kappa is stored only at grid points; any interpolation between 33 and 34 keV straddles the edge and does not reproduce the jump. Use the diagnostics above.
Ref densities are elemental reference values (I2 solid 4.93, Ca metal 1.55), not tissue-mixture densities.
Water kappa is a single compound H2O at unit density; no tissue composition is modelled.
Spectra are SpekPy native normalisation and not verified against a physical reference. Rescale before use.
Spectrum mass below 9.5 keV and above 150.5 keV is outside the grid and is dropped; fractions are in spectra.per_kvp_stats.
Spectra assume SpekPy's characteristic W lines (default char=True) and the 12 deg reflection geometry; no heel effect or detector response.
Only 2.5 mm Al filtration is modelled; no inherent tube filtration.
Data lineage of xraylib and SpekPy attenuation tables is UNVERIFIED (see database_descriptions).
